data.narrative:
Transmutex is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Franklin Servan-Schreiber, Federico Carminati, and Jean-Pierre Revol, having raised $23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 companies across public and private markets in nuclear energy, including public names trading under OKLO, NNE, and SMR, alongside private peers Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy at varying stages.

Two valuation methods were triangulated. Stage-progression analysis applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement to the $23M raised proxy, implying $46M valuation. Peer-median methodology examined three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics at Series B ($6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy at Seed ($808M), and Fuse Energy at Series A ($200M)—yielding a median of $808M and a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. This wide peer dispersion reflects stage variance and market heterogeneity within frontier nuclear.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $39M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $427M. This wide band reflects material uncertainty around Transmutex's technology risk, commercialization timeline, and capital intensity relative to peers. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to deployed capital; peer comparables suggest substantially higher values contingent on technology validation and market adoption assumptions. Key uncertainties include regulatory pathway clarity and competitive positioning within the advanced reactor segment.
